baselineAccessInitial.methodology: Serial fresh processes, rotated variants/runtime order, 100000 warmup probes, 5000000 timed probes. Identical visit order and checksums. Inner timer excludes warmup; OS counters include the full process. Synthetic controls are not full-engine speedup claims.

baselineEvidence.interpretation: Runtime and generated engine code both contribute. Generated engine includes inline guards. Collector-stack share does not include all inline GC barriers or rooting costs. Static assembly fallback calls are not proof they execute on every iteration.

researchConclusions: The original Perry excess instruction count predates all size-build changes.
App Oz plus Rust runtime Oz causes a separate performance regression. App O2 alone only partially repairs it; runtime O2 restores near-original search speed at approximately 7.4 MiB.
Replacing the system allocator with mimalloc in the Oz runtime changes search median by only about 1.2%; allocator choice does not explain the 2x residual gap.
The stock-runtime control retains original engine loops and speed settings, while avoiding renderer expansion and unneeded dependencies; 8.04 MiB and near-original search performance.
Method removal, cached class field, standalone function and Int32Array alone do not close the synthetic original-Perry gap.

Array/key/value proofs need to survive boundaries to eliminate repeated generic admission checks. TypeScript annotations alone are insufficient evidence because JS permits holes, prototype mutation and values inconsistent with annotations.
unmeasuredNextSteps: Use compiler-derived construction/assignment and integer-range proofs to specialize hot numeric kernels, hoisting array and prototype admission checks only when invalidation semantics allow it.
Reduce iterator protocol work and repeated stack/TLS/root bookkeeping, preserving exception, callback, mutation and moving-GC behavior.
Use profile-guided inlining/layout and cold-path size optimization with a speed-optimized runtime; blanket Oz is rejected.
Rebuild and benchmark upstream iterator and unrolling fixes on the full app; PR microbenchmark results do not establish a full-app speedup.
publication: User subsequently requested publication. Five issues filed: #13659–#13663; #13645 updated. No PR for the size preset.

freshProfiles.limitations: Eight-second samples at 1 ms, after one-second startup delay. Search profiles use 500000 nodes; different speeds sample different search phases. Baseline uses app Os/ABI-on, Oz-runtime diagnostic uses app O2/ABI-off. Runtime-only effects are isolated in the timing experiment, not this profile pair. Outlined fragments perform necessary work, so their sample share is not entirely removable overhead.

validation.limitations: O2/Os minimal-runtime candidates have workload parity only in this round; they are not approved release configurations.

baselineFurtherFindings: A fixed bound reduces cached-field synthetic probe from 327.73 to 256.38 ms and 5.035G to 3.440G instructions. Replacing direction reads with arithmetic reduces it further to 133.61 ms and 2.127G instructions.

The fixed-bound experiment changes the loop bound and equivalent increment spelling to avoid the compiler literal-loop unroller. It is a diagnostic source reduction, not a universally semantics-preserving array-length optimization.
Typed directions do not help: 277.66 ms versus 256.38 ms for ordinary directions with the same fixed bound.
The numeric layout helper already uses an O(1) header flag after initial setup; repeated full-array scans are not the explanation. Header/pointer/layout admission is still repeated.

One direction sample in the seven-variant run had a large walltime outlier (321.74 ms vs later 129.84/132.00 ms), without a corresponding instruction increase. Raw samples retained; final nine-variant run is separate.

runtimeBuildProfiles.scripts/perry-balanced-runtime.toml:
# Research configuration: hold minimal features and fat LTO fixed while
# changing Rust optimization from size-first to speed-first. Not a preset.
[profile.chess-balanced]
inherits = "release"
opt-level = 2
lto = "fat"
strip = false

[profile.chess-balanced.package.perry-runtime]
opt-level = 2

[profile.chess-balanced.package.perry-stdlib]
opt-level = 2
runtimeBuildProfiles.scripts/perry-runtime-os.toml:
# Research middle ground: size optimization without LLVM minsize behavior.
[profile.chess-balanced]
inherits = "release"
opt-level = "s"
lto = "fat"
strip = false

[profile.chess-balanced.package.perry-runtime]
opt-level = "s"

[profile.chess-balanced.package.perry-stdlib]
opt-level = "s"

acceptedResult: 8.04 MiB stock-runtime control retains approximately original performance across four measured workloads and passes full correctness/terminal checks. No statistical zero-regression proof; all benchmarks are on one machine.
rejectedForPerformance: 7.43 MiB app O2/runtime O2 candidate: about 1.8% slower evaluation and additional instructions
6.23 MiB app O2/runtime Os candidate: about 4.0% slower evaluation and additional instructions
